First release of NetScope, a command-line static analyzer for .NET assemblies.

## Downloads

Self-contained single-file executables; no .NET installation required.

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows x64 | `netscope-win-x64-v1.0.0.zip` |
| Windows ARM64 | `netscope-win-arm64-v1.0.0.zip` |
| Linux x64 | `netscope-linux-x64-v1.0.0.tar.gz` |
| Linux ARM64 | `netscope-linux-arm64-v1.0.0.tar.gz` |

Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The Windows x64, Windows ARM64 and Linux x64 builds are smoke-tested in CI. The Linux ARM64 build is compiled in CI but has not been run.

## What it does

For each method of one or many `.dll`/`.exe` files:

- **Methods:** kind (constructor, property, event, operator, async, iterator, lambda, local function, P/Invoke, generic, virtual/abstract/override…), signature, access, RVA and size.
- **Calls:** `call`, `callvirt`, `newobj`, `calli`, `ldftn`, `ldvirtftn` with internal/external target, plus "called by" lists and a call graph across all input files.
- **Branches:** basic blocks with conditions such as `user != null`, loops, unreachable blocks, exits, nested try/catch/filter/finally/fault regions and cyclomatic complexity.
- **Pseudocode:** C# via ICSharpCode.Decompiler, with a three-address fallback built from the IL when decompilation fails.
- **Assembly code:**
  - an ildasm-style IL listing;
  - ReadyToRun native code, including funclets and precompiled generic instantiations;
  - C++/CLI native methods;
  - JIT output from an isolated helper process, only with `--allow-run`.

Output formats: text, JSON, Graphviz DOT, Mermaid.

The analyzed code is never executed unless `--allow-run` is given. See the [README](https://github.com/rorythebreaker/netscope#readme) for usage, exit codes and known limitations.
